newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina sounds out banks on stand-by loan - Calvo.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sounds out banks on stand-by loan - Calvo.

text.p: Argentina is sounding out international banks on the possibility of acquiring a stand-by loan in case of a financial crisis, said Guilllermo Calvo, former advisor to Economy Minister Roque Fernandez.
"I know that the economy ministry is sounding out international banks...to acquire a security credit," Calvo said in an interview with daily Ambito Financiero published Thursday.

An official at the economy ministry, however, told Reuters the idea is "very good," but "for now no such loan is planned." The official did not deny that a loan of this kind "could be put into effect in the future."

Argentina has already set up a $6.0 billion stand-by loan with a group of banks led by Chase Manhattan to be used to support the banking sector in case of a financial crisis such as the "Tequila effect" which rocked Argentina in 1995.
The new stand-by loan would cover any shortfalls in state expenditure resulting from an economic shock, Calvo said.

"It would be an association with a top international financial entity that through the payment of a premium would be obliged to cover a shortfall if Argentina could not acquire funds in the financial markets," he told the newspaper.
